goal: Drive the production invoker via the SDK `ClaudeSDKClient` with a watcher coroutine that claims and applies control commands (interrupt/say/set_model) live against the open session, emits each application as an audit event, and exposes the producers through `flywheel steer/interrupt/set-model` CLI subcommands.

relevant: src/flywheel/invoker.py — invoke_iteration (lines 135-200), the one-shot query() call at :188, and the on_message observation/persistence seam to preserve
src/flywheel/workflow.py — subcommand registration; mirror existing _cmd_* patterns for steer / interrupt / set-model
src/flywheel/store_protocols.py — the control-command verbs (enqueue_command / claim_commands) the watcher and CLI consume
references: claude_agent_sdk ClaudeSDKClient — query(), interrupt(), set_model(), set_permission_mode(), receive_response(): the bidirectional API to adopt in place of the one-shot query() at invoker.py:188
src/flywheel/workflow.py — _cmd_* subcommand patterns to mirror for the new producers
src/flywheel/invoker.py:135-200 — preserve the on_message seam (00010) while opening a persistent ClaudeSDKClient connection per iteration
constraints: Preserve the on_message persistence/observation seam from 00010 and the cancellation/INTERRUPTED finalization semantics from 00012; the store-triggered interrupt shares that finalization path.
The watcher is best-effort: a failed command application is recorded as a failed-application audit event but never aborts the run, mirroring the on_message best-effort contract.
Commands are applied claim-once in enqueue order; each applied command emits its own telemetry audit event into the run's stream.
Cross-process only via the store: producers and the consuming watcher share no process state, so flywheel steer works against a detached worker daemon.
The task definition stays immutable; steering affects the running session only.
Keep flywheel.task and flywheel.lifecycle purity untouched.
Run mcp__ide__getDiagnostics on every .py file touched and fix all Pylance errors in the same turn.
Commit with a Conventional Commits `feat:` message before emitting intent=verify.
non_goals: No auto-steering or policy-driven intervention; operator-driven CLI only.
No web/socket transport; the channel is the store.
No changes to graders or validation.
No edits to the immutable task definition.
edge_cases: Command targets a run that is not currently in-flight: it is never applied to a different run and does not crash.
client.interrupt() / set_model() raises: record a failed-application audit event; do not abort the stream.
Watcher briefly loses the store connection: retry on the next tick; claim-once prevents double-apply.
Command enqueued after the iteration ended: not applied to a completed iteration; remains for the next eligible iteration or is recorded as stale per claim semantics.
set_model to an invalid model: application fails -> failed-application audit event; the run continues on the prior model.
interrupt via this channel vs SIGINT (00012): both reach INTERRUPTED via the same finalization; the store-triggered path additionally records a control event.
